did: The phone app's launch test had gone red on every release since the Cast wing landed: the test emulator vanished right after Cast opened. I made the test say which step it died on, then used four approved test runs to find the cause. Painting the cast's drawings under the emulator's default software renderer kills the emulator; drawing them differently did not help, taking them out did. The launch test and the compatibility runs now use a different renderer, ANGLE over SwiftShader, and in that run the emulator got through Cast. Along the way the Cast previews stopped decoding about ninety images a second, and the monkey walk no longer fails on a hang in Android's own windows while an app hang still fails it.

calls.title: The launch test visits the wings in a fixed order, Cast last, after a drag at the foyer
options: Fixed order by name, Z to A, with a foyer drag first
calls.why: A fixed order makes two runs of one build take the same steps, and the foyer drag tests the first drag after boot with no wing involved, which is what told the two suspects apart.
calls.undo: Drop the sort and the foyer drag in apps/mobile/launch/launch-test.sh.

calls.title: The monkey walk is capped at ten minutes
calls.why: With hangs ignored, a hung app could walk until the job's 30 minute timeout, and the checks that catch an app hang would never run.
calls.undo: Remove timeout 600 before adb shell monkey in apps/mobile/launch/launch-test.sh.

left: The fix is not yet proven on main: the next Mobile APK run, after the owner approves the mobile-release environment, is the proof.
Whether the Cast wing draws fine on a real phone is unverified until the owner opens it there.
snips-capture.yml still uses swiftshader_indirect; only the two approved workflows changed, and its Cast captures could hit the same crash.
The storm scenario's joined phase failed once with no baseline, filed as some-ui#3617.
